candidates.review_note: For candidate period k, each residue class contains q or q+1 positions with q=floor((a+b)/k). The number of A classes must be between ceil(a/(q+1)) and floor(a/q), with the analogous bounds for B classes; their sum must equal k. With both letters present, a feasible class allocation can be arranged as a primitive block with the prescribed longer prefix counts, so these are exactly the possible minimal periods. Count the intersection of these bounds over equal-quotient intervals in O(sqrt(a+b)); exhaustive all binary strings through length15 independently checks the minimal-period rather than merely periodicity interpretation.

Undirected vertex geography is losing for the next mover exactly at vertices that can be unmatched in a maximum matching. AA chooses the start but YY moves first, so those losing-next-mover vertices are AA winning starts. Compute a bipartite maximum matching of the passable grid; alternating paths from unmatched vertices on each side identify every same-side vertex that can become unmatched. Preserve isolated cells and list the union in row-major order. Public brute force explores the complete visited-set game independently.
